author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Harness signal registry: identity detection becomes declared data that a config entry or a package can extend without a code change

Harness detection is currently two hardcoded arrays in src/core/shared/author.ts — HARNESS_ENV_MARKERS with seven entries and HARNESS_TOKEN_MARKERS with seven regexes — plus an inline CI branch. Adding a harness, or teaching pm where a known harness publishes its model, requires editing core source, rebuilding, and shipping a release. That is the wrong shape for a surface whose contents change whenever the agent ecosystem changes, and it contradicts the universal-customization promise: a workspace running an in-house harness cannot make pm recognize it at all. Convert the table to declared data with the same purity guarantees: a signal descriptor names the harness, the environment keys that identify it, the environment keys that carry its model and session, and an optional bounded argv pattern. Built-in descriptors ship as data; workspace settings and packages may append descriptors; built-ins are never silently overridden — a conflicting descriptor is a validation error, not a last-writer-wins race. Precedence within the registry is declared and stable, so adding an entry cannot reorder detection for existing harnesses.

Built-in harness descriptors are declared data with a documented schema covering harness slug, identifying environment keys, model-carrying keys, session-carrying keys, and optional bounded argv patterns; Workspace settings and installed packages can append descriptors, and a descriptor that collides with a built-in slug fails validation with a named error instead of overriding it silently; Detection precedence is declared and stable, proven by a test asserting that appending a descriptor cannot change the result for any previously supported harness; The registry is exercised by a test that registers a synthetic harness and observes correct harness, model, and session resolution end to end; Descriptors stay pure data: no descriptor may specify a command to execute, a path to traverse, or a network endpoint, enforced by schema validation
Recognizing a new agent harness is a configuration change, not a pm release
The agent-harness ecosystem changes faster than pm's release cadence; a hardcoded table guarantees pm is permanently behind it
Moves seven hardcoded entries into declared data with a validation contract; no behavior change for currently supported harnesses
A team running an unlisted or in-house harness gets correct identity provenance without waiting for an upstream release

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Acceptance finding and fix: a tracker evidence comment containing a harness name exposed that scanning every CLI argument could misclassify ordinary free text as a harness signal. Detection now bounds argv identity/model markers to the executable launch prefix (first three tokens); explicit process_labels remain the host-controlled extension seam. A regression test proves a later claude-code-agent comment value cannot spoof detection.
